newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat phones Netanyahu after Jordan attack.
newsitem.headline: Arafat phones Netanyahu after Jordan attack.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat telephoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday to express condolences over the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier.
The telephone call, reported by Netanyahu's spokesman, was the first contact between the two leaders since Arafat angrily rejected last week a planned Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank.

"The chairman of the Palestinian Authority, Yasser Arafat, called Prime Minister Netanyahu this evening and expressed his sorrow over the event at Naharayim and asked him to convey his condolences to the families," spokesman Shai Bazak said.
Before the call, Arafat aide Marwan Kanafani raised the possibility of a meeting between Netanyahu and the Palestinian president.

"The president is willing to meet Netanyahu if the meeting is to discuss the latest Israeli measures, including the settlement in (Arab East Jerusalem) and (West Bank) redeployment," Marwan Kanafani told Reuters.
Palestinian officials and Jordan's King Hussein had warned about the possibility of bloodshed if Israel went ahead with plans to build 6,500 more homes for Jews between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
Bazak quoted Netanyahu as telling Arafat in the telephone call: "There can be differences of opinion but there is no place for all the talk about violence."

Israel-PLO relations plunged further when the Israeli government announced last week that a West Bank pullback, one of three due to be completed by mid-1998, would be only a third of the size demanded by the PLO.

Israel said that senior Palestine Liberation Organisation official Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, phoned Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to express condolences over the killing on the Jordanian border. "He said that 'this an event of extreme gravity which touches the heart of all of us because innocent children were the victims'," Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Danny Shek quoted Abu Mazen as saying.

Abu Mazen, architect of the 1993 Israel-PLO self-rule deal and chief Palestinian negotiator with Israel, tendered his resignation to Arafat in protest at Israel's moves on settlement and redeployment. Arafat has yet to decide whether to accept the resignation.
